BUILDING THE FUTURE OF AFRICAN LIVESTOCK

Poultry nutrition: forecasting, causal evidence and tested controls

Executed analysis and interpretation

Analysis run 1395afb10eb726ef | Public-data research | 200 months · 63 pens

What the completed analysis found

The preselected forecasts did not beat the baseline. The development-selected models had slightly higher holdout MAE than the previous-month baseline. In the trial, none of the six FCR contrasts was significant after Holm correction. The LowCP-NoSBM diet reduced daily gain by 4.52 g/bird/day (95% CI -7.09 to -1.95; Holm p=0.0052). This is a whole-diet effect, subject to the public-data design limitations.

Executed in R, with independent Python verification. All 200 selected months and all 63 performance pens are complete. Thirteen internal control tests passed. This report presents two separate studies; it does not join US market ratios to Canadian animal outcomes or claim African effect sizes.

1. Sources and validation

USDA ERS Yearbook Table 15: workbook dated 13 October 2026, January 2010-August 2026 selected. The ratio is pounds of broiler-grower feed equal in value to one pound of live broiler. Higher means stronger feed purchasing power relative to bird value.

Randomized trial: article DOI; data DOI. Trial conducted in Quebec, Canada in 2022, with seven whole-diet treatments and nine pens per treatment. CT is control; MedCP/LowCP denote crude-protein reductions of approximately 15/30 g/kg from control; High/Med/NoSBM denote soybean-meal sourcing strategies. Experimental diets were fed over days 11-35.

2. Time structure and model development

Initial training: January 2010-December 2017. Development targets end August 2024. Holdout targets: September 2024-August 2026. Models are refitted on expanding histories for 1- and 3-month forecasts. Selection uses development MAE only. Fifteen fixed model specifications cover ARMA, ARIMA, SARIMA, ETS and simple baselines. ETS means Error, Trend, Seasonal.

ADF and KPSS diagnostics on development data support first differencing. Neither test establishes an immutable data-generating process. The decomposition is descriptive and is not computed over future observations for forecasting features.

3. Held-out forecast performance

Each reported horizon has 24 holdout targets. Errors are in ratio units. Selected ETS(AAA) has 1-month MAE 0.2401 versus naive 0.2333. Selected SARIMA(0,1,1)(0,1,1)[12] has 3-month MAE 0.4451 versus naive 0.4167. These comparisons do not establish statistically significant superiority; they show that this model-selection exercise did not improve the primary holdout metric.

Seven fitting failures occurred in other candidate models and were logged. Models with incomplete development forecasts were ineligible for selection. The single-vintage backtest does not reconstruct historical release delays or revisions, and 3-month errors overlap.

4. Causal estimand and trial findings

Experimental unit: pen. Primary outcome: FCR during days 11-35; secondary: daily gain during the same period. Effects are treatment minus CT, adjusted for centered pretreatment body weight. HC3 standard errors and residual-degrees-of-freedom t confidence intervals are used. Six comparisons within each endpoint receive Holm correction; intervals are pointwise 95%, not simultaneous.

Randomization supports causal interpretation of the assigned ration under consistency and no relevant between-pen interference. Block IDs are absent from the public data, so this analysis does not replicate the published blocked model. Other formulation components change with protein and soybean-meal strategies; isolated protein or amino-acid effects cannot be identified.

5. Longitudinal and sensitivity evidence

Two deposited phases per pen produce 126 linked observations. Mixed models use pen random intercepts and phase-specific residual variances. Treatment-by-phase interaction is supported for ADG (exploratory p=0.0037), but not FCR (p=0.1547). These are phase-level measurements, not daily time-series data.

The supporting 54-pen CP-by-SBM FCR interaction has HC3 Wald p=0.2248. In all 63 leave-one-pen-out analyses, the LowCP-NoSBM ADG estimate remains negative and its Holm p stays below 0.023. This sensitivity does not recover missing blocks or establish generalizability.

6. Governance, risk and internal audit

The project organizes governance evidence around NIST AI RMF 1.0: Govern, Map, Measure and Manage. The risk register distinguishes controls implemented and tested from future deployment proposals. There is no live AI service or automated feeding/procurement system.

Data-integrity, calendar, pen identity, label, leakage and stale-output controls were challenged with invalid inputs. All 13 positive/negative tests passed. Independent Python calculations reproduce R treatment estimates, SEs, confidence intervals and raw p values to within numerical precision, and verify forecast arithmetic, selection, run IDs and hashes.

Remaining limitations include missing trial blocks, regional transfer, possible data revisions, model residual dependence, unscreened software vulnerabilities, and untested production access control/rollback. Full details and evidence references are in the risk register and governance document.

7. Practical deductions and publication sequence

Retain a simple forecast baseline in every procurement planning review. Evaluate feed purchasing power separately from biological feed efficiency. Do not promise that protein reduction preserves performance merely because FCR differences were not significant. In African systems, link dated ingredient prices and lab assays to formulations, batches, pen feed records, weights, health and carcass outcomes before claiming local forecast or treatment benefits.

Four-day sequence: (1) what feed records measure; (2) whether forecasting complexity helps; (3) what the randomized ration comparison shows; (4) sensitivity and governance evidence. Use the actual R figures, one main result per slide, with light backgrounds and no green. The campaign expression Potential × Management × System = Performance remains conceptual, not a fitted model.

R code, raw snapshots, cleaned data, tables, PNG/PDF charts, fitted objects, console logs, Python verification, risk and claims registers are bundled. Re-run instructions and methodological boundaries are in README.md.
